task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

- **Line 555-123-2002 (L1002)** — Active, on the **Premium Plan** (15 GB data limit, $65/month)
- **Current data usage:** 15.1 GB out of 15.0 GB — **you've exceeded your plan's data limit**

To get your data working again on this line, you have two options:

turns.execution_output:
User: Oh, a reboot? That makes me a bit nervous... I have so many photos of my grandchildren on this phone. Will restarting it delete any of my pictures? I don't want to lose those. 

And about the payment — could we maybe sort out the internet first, and do the payment after? I just want to make sure it's actually working before I pay for anything.

turns.thought:
That's completely understandable — let me put your mind at ease.

**Regarding the reboot:** Restarting your phone simply powers it down and starts it back up. Per our troubleshooting guide, it "restarts your phone completely" and refreshes all the running services and connections — it fixes software glitches. It doesn't make any changes to your line, your plan, or your data allowance. Your photos are stored on the device, and a restart doesn't touch them.

**Regarding the payment:** Absolutely, we'll hold off. You're not obligated to pay anything right now, and I won't send a payment request without your say-so. We can do that later once you've confirmed your data is working properly.

Please go ahead and reboot your device now, and then try your mobile data — open a webpage or an app that needs internet. If the connection is restored and working well, we're done, and you can let me know whenever you'd like to take care of the payment.

If it's **still** not working after the reboot, come back to me and I'll help you dig into other possible causes, such as:
- Data Saver mode being on
- Airplane mode
- An active VPN slowing things down
- Your network mode preference setting

Just let me know how it goes after the restart.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, if you're sure it won't touch my photos... I'll try it. Give me a moment.

turns.thought:
No, you haven't broken anything! That airplane symbol means **Airplane Mode is ON** — it's a setting on your phone that turns off all wireless connections (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth). It sometimes gets switched on by accident during a restart or by an accidental tap.

Let's check your phone's current network status so I can confirm what's going on before guiding you to fix it.

Please use the **check_network_status** tool on your device and let me know what it reports.

Once you've done that, the fix is straightforward — use **toggle_airplane_mode** to turn Airplane Mode OFF, and your cellular connection and mobile data should come back.

Go ahead and run that check, and tell me what it shows.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me check that for you. One moment...

turns.thought:
You're right that it's not good, but it's also very easy to fix. Here's what's happening: **Airplane Mode being ON is the cause of everything else you're seeing.** With Airplane Mode on, your phone disconnects all wireless radios — which is exactly why you have "no service," no signal, mobile data off, and Wi-Fi off. The good news is your SIM card is **active**, which means your SIM is working fine and nothing is broken.

**Please do this now:**
Use the **toggle_airplane_mode** tool on your device to turn Airplane Mode **OFF**.

After you do that, please use **check_network_status** again and tell me what it shows. I expect your signal strength, cellular service, and mobile data should all come back — and your Wi-Fi too, if you want it on.

Let me know how it goes.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, I'll turn that airplane thing off now.

turns.thought:
That's great progress — you're connected with excellent signal on 5G, so your service is fully restored. 

The "Mobile Data Enabled: No" just means the **mobile data switch** on your phone is still turned off. It's a separate setting from Airplane Mode, and turning Airplane Mode off didn't automatically switch it back on. It's not a problem with your account or your line — it's just a toggle on the device.

Also worth noting: the underlying issue (being over your 15 GB limit) **has** been fixed — your line now has 2 GB refueled on top of the allowance, so once this switch is on, your data should work.

**Please do this now:**
Use the **toggle_data** tool on your device to turn mobile data **ON**.

Then use **check_network_status** again to confirm it now shows mobile data enabled.

Optional: Wi-Fi is also still off on your phone. If you'd like Wi-Fi back as well, use **toggle_wifi** to turn it on — it's not required for your mobile data to work, though.

Let me know what it shows afterward. If data is then working reliably, we're all set — and we can leave the payment for whenever you're ready.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, turning the mobile data on now.

turns.thought:
Yes, you should absolutely do something about that — you've spotted the likely cause of the slowness.

**Data Saver mode restricts background data usage and can make apps and services seem slow or unresponsive.** That matches the "very slow" part of what you were experiencing, so turning it off should help.

Also, turning it off won't cost you anything or change your plan — and it won't delete any of your photos or other data on the phone.

**Please do this:**
1. First, use **check_data_restriction_status** on your device to confirm Data Saver is on.
2. If it confirms it's on (as the icon suggests), use **toggle_data_saver_mode** to turn it **OFF**.

After that, try loading a webpage or using an app that needs the internet, and check the status bar again to confirm the Data Saver icon is gone.

Let me know how it goes — and remember, we'll leave the payment until you're happy everything's working.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check that first, then.

turns.thought:
Yes, there's a proper way to test it.

**Please use the `run_speed_test` tool on your device.** This measures your current internet connection speed (download speed) and tells you the connection quality — it'll report as "unknown," "very poor," "poor," "fair," "good," or "excellent," and it also lets you know what activities the speed can support (like browsing, streaming, etc.).

That will give you a real, measured answer rather than just relying on the icons at the top of your screen.

Run that test and tell me what it reports. If the result comes back below "excellent," let me know and I'll help you look at other possible causes — for example, I can check whether a VPN is active and slowing things down, or check your network mode preference.

Once you're satisfied the speed is genuinely good, we can take care of the payment — but only then, at your pace.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me run that speed test.

turns.thought:
Don't worry — nothing has been undone. Your status bar shows a good 5G connection, and I've just re-checked your line on my end: it's **Active**, with no suspension, and the 2 GB refuel is confirmed applied (2.0 GB refueling on your account). So your account and line are in good shape.

This means the "No Connection" is coming from something on the phone's settings side. There are a few likely culprits, and we can check them one at a time.

**Please do this first — the most likely cause:**
Use **check_apn_settings** on your device and tell me what it reports.

APN (Access Point Name) settings are what your phone uses to actually connect to the carrier's mobile data network. If they're incorrect, you can have full 5G signal showing but still have no working data — exactly what you're describing. Please also tell me whether it shows an MMSC URL.

If the APN is incorrect, the fix is to use **reset_apn_settings**, and then **reboot_device** for the changes to take effect.

Let me know what the APN check shows and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me check those settings. I don't really understand what they are, but I'll do it.

turns.thought:
Good news — those APN settings **look correct**. The APN name is set to "internet" and the MMSC URL is properly configured (that's the server address used for picture messaging). So the APN is not the problem, and you were right to leave it unchanged. I won't ask you to reset it.

Let's move to the next most likely cause.

**Please use `check_vpn_status` on your device and tell me what it shows.**

A VPN (a private network connection) can sometimes be active without you realizing it, and a slow or misconfigured VPN can block or throttle your data — you'd still show 5G signal but have no usable connection.

- If it says a VPN is **ON and connected** (especially with poor performance), we'll use **disconnect_vpn** to turn it off.
- If it says the VPN is **off**, we'll rule that out and check your **network mode preference** next, plus re-check your data restriction status, since sometimes a setting can flip back.

Run that check and let me know what it reports. We'll get to the bottom of it.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, checking that VPN thing now.

turns.thought:
I understand — let's keep going. We've ruled out the APN and the VPN. Your line is Active with the refuel applied, so this is a device-side setting.

**Next, please use `check_network_mode_preference` on your device and tell me what it shows.**

This tells us which cellular network technology your phone prefers to connect to. If it's set to something like "2G" or "3G," that's an older, much slower technology and can cause exactly the crawling/no-connection behavior you're describing — even while the icon at the top still shows a network.

- If it shows **2G or 3G**, we'll use `set_network_mode_preference` with the mode **"4g_5g_preferred"** so your phone can connect to the fast networks.
- If it already shows 4G/5G, we'll rule that out and look at the remaining possibilities.

Run that check and let me know. We have a few avenues left, so don't worry — we'll get there.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, checking that now.

turns.thought: I understand your frustration — let me check one more thing on my end before I ask you to do anything else.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry this has dragged on — let's keep at it. Your account and line are fine (the line is Active, the 2 GB refuel is confirmed on your account, and your APN, VPN, and network mode are all correct). So we're looking for a device-side cause, and there's one important one we haven't checked yet.

**Please use `check_sim_status` on your device and tell me what it reports.**

The SIM card is the card that contains your information and lets your phone connect to the cellular network — if it isn't properly seated, it can cause loss of service or data. This is worth checking because I can see on your account that there was activity on this device recently: it was activated on **2025-02-15**, and it has eSIM capability with an eSIM transfer recorded on **2025-01-20**. That kind of recent change can sometimes leave things not quite settled.

- If it shows **"Missing"**, we'll use `reseat_sim_card` to correctly reseat it.
- If it shows **"Locked"** (from incorrect PIN/PUK entries), I'll need to escalate you to technical support for SIM security.
- If it shows **"Active"**, the SIM is fine and we'll move on to the next step.

Let me know what it says, John. We still have options left — you won't be left stuck with this.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me check the SIM card.

turns.thought:
I hear your frustration, John, and it's completely justified — but please don't give up yet. Let me explain where we stand, because it's actually useful information:

**Everything on your account and line is confirmed working.** Your line is Active with no suspension, your 2 GB refuel is applied, your SIM is active, your signal is excellent on 5G, and your APN, VPN, and network mode settings are all correct. So the problem is narrowed down to a setting on the phone itself — and we haven't yet re-checked the phone's *overall current state* since we made all those changes.

That's important: settings can flip back. Earlier, Airplane Mode turned itself on after a restart, so I don't want to assume everything we changed has stuck.

**Please use `check_status_bar` on your device and tell me everything it shows** — particularly:
- The signal strength and network technology (e.g. 5G)
- Whether it says "Data Enabled" or "Data Disabled"
- Whether the Data Saver icon appears
- Whether Airplane Mode has crept back on
- The Wi-Fi and VPN status

This gives us the full current picture in one go, rather than checking things piecemeal. Once I can see the complete state, I can pinpoint what's still out of place.

If everything there looks right, the next step is to reboot the device once more, since all the changes we've made together need a refresh to fully settle — and as we established, a restart won't touch your photos.

Run that check and let me know exactly what it reports. We'll get this sorted.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me look at the top of my screen and tell you everything.

turns.thought:
Yes, absolutely — that's exactly the right next step. The speed test failed *before* we turned off Data Saver and disabled Airplane Mode, so that result is out of date. Your status bar now shows everything in good order: excellent signal, 5G, data enabled, no Airplane Mode, no Data Saver.

**Please run `run_speed_test` again** and tell me what it reports this time.

If it comes back with a proper speed reading (anything from "fair" up to "excellent"), then your connection is genuinely working and we're done — the earlier failure was simply because Data Saver was throttling your data.

If it still says "No Connection," let me know, and the next step is a **reboot of the device** to let all the changes we've made fully take effect. I'll remind you again that a restart won't delete your photos or anything else on the phone.

Go ahead and run it — fingers crossed.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, here goes. Running the speed test again.

turns.thought:

That combination tells me the remaining cause is something on the device itself that I can't reach or resolve with the tools I have — and I don't want to keep putting you through checks that all come back "fine" while your internet stays broken.
